rows.quote: Does the benchmark address a meaningful gap or enable reliable comparison across methods? Does it change how we measure progress in this area?
rows.status_note: a crowded field: 53 related benchmarks and methods in the survey
rows.fix: Lead with one finding: how often agents are right for the wrong reasons, and where the step-score ranking disagrees with the final-answer ranking. Then run the step grading on SPAR-Bench, a real benchmark that ships depth and camera poses per item, to show conclusions shift on an existing benchmark.
rows.effort: build 2-3 days; GPU part of the main runs + ~10-20 h for SPAR-Bench (~$10-20), estimate

rows.quote: Originality may be achieved through novel task design, evaluation setup, or analysis that reveals properties of existing benchmarks. Beating a baseline is not required.
rows.status_note: audited 2026-09-30: 2 claims survive only narrowed; 2 of 4 proposed metrics taken or decoration
rows.fix: Claim only what survived the audit: (1) per-step grading of continuous 3D quantities and tool outputs against exact state, (2) camera-pose twins scored as pairs. Cite Theory of Space, WebStep, EqBen, NaturalBench, MetaSpace, Lanham and FRODO, CanTest as the closest work; re-audit before submission.

rows.quote: Evaluate the rigor of task design, item selection, and evaluation setup. Assess whether benchmark saturation or overfitting is adequately addressed.
rows.status_note: no blind text-only check, error bars or label audit yet
rows.fix: (1) Run a text-only model and prune items it answers without the images. (2) Twins cancel guessing by design: one 3D change flips the answer. (3) Error bars clustered by twin pair. (4) Humans check 300 random items; unit tests for every checker. (5) Public dev split, private test split minted from a secret seed, so the test cannot be memorised.
rows.effort: build 3-4 days; GPU ~5 h text-only pass (~$5); 6-8 person-hours for the label check, estimate

rows.quote: (Not quoted in the guidelines; closest:) Is the submission technically sound, and are the claims well-supported by empirical, analytical, or conceptual arguments?
rows.status_note: do scores on renders mean anything for real photos? the biggest risk
rows.fix: (1) Real-to-sim pairs: film a few real rooms or aisles on a phone, rebuild them as photoreal 3D scenes (Gaussian splatting), ask the same questions on the real photos and on the renders. (2) Rank 10+ models on our test and on OmniSpatial, MMSI and ViewSpatial; report rank correlation. (3) Tool check: depth and mask errors on renders match the same tools on real photos.
rows.effort: build 1-2 weeks (capture, reconstruction, paired questions); GPU ~20-40 h (~$20-40), estimate

rows.quote: Benchmark construction, task design choices, and evaluation protocols are clearly described and reproducible. Could another team re-run the benchmark from this paper?
rows.status_note: no public host, harness or fixed split yet
rows.fix: Ship pre-rendered images plus truth files (no Isaac Sim needed to evaluate), a VLMEvalKit plug-in, a pinned environment and seeds, and the generator code.
